correctness.rationale: Sylvester’s gap parametrization converts gaps of <a,b>/p into positive lattice points (i,j) with p|(ab−ia−jb). The PF condition is coordinatewise minimality; the large-generator hypothesis a,b≥2p+1 makes every point in the unit-residue box [1,p]^2 positive. Unit conditions produce affine permutation j_i≡a−(ab^{-1})i (mod p); its left-to-right record minima count type. If R=p−N, at least p−3N−1 adjacent-position record transitions have value drop one, strictly positive when 3N+2≤p; hence step is −1 modulo p and a≡b. The descending initial run then has length p−N iff a≡b≡1−N, proving both directions. N=1 forces forbidden zero residue. Independently checked all 18,368 ordered unit-residue pairs for p=5..50 against all stated near-maximal criteria and penultimate exclusion.

An undiscovered corollary of the general formulas remains a residual risk.

value.rationale: The type of a numerical semigroup is an intrinsic Cohen–Macaulay invariant, and forbidding p−1 while classifying every near-maximal type by one residue pair is a structural restriction across arbitrarily many moduli and generators. This is more than computing finitely many individual PF sets and may guide high-type constructions; it does not claim a complete type spectrum.
